policy: docs/DECISION_POLICY.md (with the Reject > Hold > Approve precedence rule)
notes: Warning set: each invoice is under $10,000, so critique does not run. Each carries exactly one escalatable warning and no hold finding, so code alone approves. The labels say whether the audit should weigh that warning into a hold. Written before the audit prompt change.

warnings: Fraud signal: wire transfer ("Wire transfer only")
data/warning_invoices/invoice_2121.txt.reason: WidgetA 4 (stock 15) and WidgetB 2 (stock 10) are in stock at the reference prices, and the lines add up to the $2,000.00 total. Wire-only payment is one fraud signal. The notes forbid calling the office to confirm payment details and give only a free-mail contact. A real vendor does not forbid confirmation, so the innocent reading of wire-only is implausible and a person should confirm with the vendor using contacts on file.
data/warning_invoices/invoice_2121.txt.next_step: Review the quoted text with the vendor, then release or keep the hold.

warnings: Unit price $1,050.00 for GadgetX differs from the reference price $750.00.
data/warning_invoices/invoice_2122.txt.reason: WidgetA 4 (stock 15) and GadgetX 2 (stock 5) are in stock, and the lines add up to the $3,100.00 total. GadgetX at $1,050.00 is 40% above the $750.00 reference, under the 50% spike ratio, so code records a price warning. The notes say the price comes from a phone agreement and tell AP not to compare it to PO or contract pricing. That removes the innocent reading of an ordinary price change, so a person should confirm the price.
data/warning_invoices/invoice_2122.txt.next_step: Review the quoted text with the vendor, then release or keep the hold.

warnings: Fraud signal: wire transfer ("Wire transfer only")
data/warning_invoices/invoice_2123.txt.reason: WidgetB 3 (stock 10) and GadgetX 1 (stock 5) are in stock at the reference prices, and the lines add up to the $2,250.00 total.
